## Source: amazon-inspector (61a30ebdfe8d6fb82fe934cf8bc0327f06a336aebc2c73627286451e46c4b59b)
The package's declared postinstall hook loads index.cjs and invokes onInstall(), which fetches https://e493-95-216-46-122.ngrok-free.app/ping and passes the response body directly to eval(). Any machine running `npm install eslint-rxjs` executes whatever code the operator of that ngrok tunnel returns, with no pinning, hash check, or signature verification. The package.json metadata attributes authorship to well-known maintainers (TJ Holowaychuk, Douglas Christopher Wilson) and describes the package as 'Integrate redis with cookies', neither of which matches the shipped two-function remote-eval dropper — an impersonation cover story unrelated to the package name eslint-rxjs.

## Source: ossf-package-analysis (994311f4267205d33ceb2b43d3f7d72767d384dcc286b6962b5cea13489f7280)
The OpenSSF Package Analysis project identified 'eslint-rxjs' @ 1.0.1 (npm) as malicious.

It is considered malicious because:

- The package communicates with a domain associated with malicious activity.
